market_name: Will 11 Fed rate cuts happen in 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the probability spike in the 11-cut market is corroborated by moves in near-term cut markets (1-3 cuts) and fed funds futures; isolated tail-market noise should be discounted.
time_plan.1h: Compare TLT and 2Y/10Y yield moves against any macro headline (payrolls shock, financial-stability event) that could justify an emergency-cut narrative.
time_plan.2h: Reassess if MOVE index / rate vol is rising; confirm whether the easing repricing is broad-based or just this single thin market.
time_plan.6h: Check for official Fed communications, data surprises, or risk-off flows into Treasuries; fade the signal if no corroboration.
time_plan.12h: Evaluate whether TLT held any gain and whether short-rate futures moved; log outcome vs. the tail-event hypothesis.

predictions.reasoning: A market pricing 11 Fed cuts (275bps) in 2026 is an extreme-tail, emergency/recession scenario. If its implied probability jumped sharply, it would reflect expectations of aggressive, possibly emergency, easing — which pulls the entire rate curve lower and sends duration-sensitive Treasuries higher. TLT is the cleanest liquid proxy for falling long-end yields.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Verify the DXY is softening and real yields (TIPS) are falling alongside the cut-expectation jump.
time_plan.1h: Check gold vs. dollar correlation; confirm move is macro-driven, not idiosyncratic metals flow.
time_plan.2h: Reassess if risk-off/safe-haven demand is present across gold, Treasuries, and JPY.
time_plan.6h: Watch for any Fed-speak or data that validates or kills the deep-easing narrative.
time_plan.12h: Log whether GLD gain persisted and whether the cut-expectation move held or reversed.

predictions.reasoning: Pricing of 11 cuts implies collapsing real rates and a dovish/crisis Fed, both classically bullish for gold as a non-yielding hedge and dollar-debasement play. GLD is a liquid proxy. Exposure is indirect and the market is a noisy tail sensor, so confidence is low.

evidence_used: Market question implies 11 cuts = 275bps of easing in 2026, an extreme-tail outcome
Fed easing cycles lower the yield curve, supporting Treasuries and gold and pressuring the dollar
Description notes emergency/inter-meeting cuts count, reinforcing the crisis interpretation of a high strike
uncertainty_notes: This is a deep tail market; implied probability is tiny and extremely noisy, so moves may be liquidity artifacts rather than information
The 700bps tradability threshold is far above any plausible 12h move in these proxies — this is NOT tradable
Mislabeled primary topic (military_conflict) suggests metadata noise; mapping rests only on the literal question

llm_justification.summary: The market asks whether the Fed delivers 11 rate cuts (~275bps) in 2026 — an extreme easing/recession tail. A sharp rise in this probability would signal expectations of aggressive or emergency easing, which would lift long Treasuries (TLT) and gold (GLD) while weighing on the dollar. However, this is a thin tail market and a noisy sensor; expected 12h moves (~50-60bps) fall far below the 700bps tradability bar, so confidence is low and neither prediction is tradable.
key_assumptions: A probability spike reflects genuine deep-easing expectations rather than thin-market noise
Treasuries and gold respond to broad easing/crisis repricing in the stated direction
No offsetting shock (e.g., inflation scare) distorts the rate reaction
failure_modes: The tail-market move is pure illiquidity noise with no macro information content
The easing expectation is already public and fully priced into bonds/gold, leaving no residual move
Proxies are weakly or ambiguously exposed over a 12h window; a crisis could also spike the dollar (safe-haven), undercutting the gold/USD-down thesis
Move reverses as the tail probability mean-reverts toward near-zero
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
